subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should the remaining fix preserve the shared Codex app-server client with stronger lease/failover semantics, or should one-shot Codex runs move to isolated clients with an explicit OpenClaw-native transcript fallback contract?
rationale: The source evidence proves the current paths still exist, but the durable fix crosses app-server lifecycle ownership, Active Memory one-shot behavior, and cross-provider transcript semantics; automation should not choose that product boundary alone.

options.title: Fix lifecycle and fallback together
options.body: Define the shared-client lease invariant, add an OpenClaw-native transcript fallback for failover, and treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99575 as only the first missing-history symptom fix.

options.title: Land warning fix first
options.body: Merge the missing-file history handling from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99575 and keep this issue open for the shared-client and failover behavior.

options.title: Isolate one-shot clients
options.body: Move ephemeral Codex one-shot runs onto dedicated clients so cleanup cannot retire the shared client, then separately decide transcript handoff behavior.

recommendation.title: Fix lifecycle and fallback together
recommendation.body: Define the shared-client lease invariant, add an OpenClaw-native transcript fallback for failover, and treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99575 as only the first missing-history symptom fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The older Codex app-server lifecycle history points to steipete as the strongest available routing candidate for the shared-client and harness boundary decision.
